summary: Streaming inference sessions stall / time out for APAC dedicated customer due to path MTU fragmentation failures
description: Issue summary: Beginning 2026-03-05 07:40 UTC, FikaHealth reported repeated streaming inference sessions that stalled mid-response and ultimately timed out. Impact: Customer-facing chat experiences experienced partial or full message loss and 30s+ tail latencies for ~40% of streaming requests from APAC clients to their Dedicated capacity. Environment: Dedicated pool in ap-southeast-1 routing through our managed NAT + transit provider peering to us-west-2 where backend model replicas live. Steps to reproduce: 1) From an APAC client network behind FikaHealth NAT, open streaming chat request to model redwood-chat-1 pinned on their dedicated pool. 2) Send a prompt that produces first streamed chunk > 1400 bytes (typical multi-paragraph reply). 3) Observe that the client receives some initial bytes then stalls for >10s before TCP retransmits lead to connection reset and request timeout. Observed symptoms: - High counts of TCP retransmits and duplicate ACKs in tcpdump at our ingress proxy. - Server-side logs show streaming generator continued producing tokens but send() blocked on socket write (backpressure). - No 5xx from model runtime; health checks stayed green. - Increase in p99/p999 latency and client-observed timeouts (sockets closed after client-side 30s). Logs/snippets: "tcp_retransmits=12; dup_acks=7; write_block_duration_ms=12040"; client traceID=fh-12345-20260305. Investigation notes: - Initial hypotheses tested: serving runtime backpressure, model CPU/GPU saturation, proxy memory leak. Metrics and traces ruled these out: GPUs < 60% util, steady request queue depth. - Packet captures from ingress (ap-southeast-1) showed IP fragments with "fragment offset" set but remote side not ACKing full segments; ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages absent. - Transit provider reported a maintenance window coinciding with the start time where a new firewall/VPN appliance was inserted with MTU set to 1400 but no MSS clamping. - PMTU discovery appears to have failed because ICMP type 3/code 4 responses were dropped by an intermediate NAT/firewall, producing a PMTU blackhole for TCP flows that attempted to send large segments. - Because our streaming implementation sends chunks near ethernet MTU (large single writes), socket writes produce large packets which then get dropped or fragmented but never reassembled due to missing PMTU signals. - A smaller reproduction: forcing chunk size <= 1200 bytes avoided stalls consistently. Temporary mitigations applied: - Immediately rolled out a streaming chunk size cap to 1200 bytes for the dedicated pool serving FikaHealth (config change deployed 2026-03-05 11:05 UTC). - Enabled application-level TCP keepalive tune and reduced socket write timeout to fail-fast for stuck streams. - Opened ticket with transit provider to restore MTU to 1500 or enable MSS clamping on the egress VPN appliance. Root cause: A new transit firewall/VPN appliance with an MTU of 1400 was added during maintenance and did not advertise PMTU or perform MSS clamping. This led to a PMTU blackhole for large TCP segments used by our streaming implementation, causing retransmits, socket stalls, and client-observed timeouts. Post-incident actions: - Provider reconfigured appliance to support PMTU/ICMP or to apply MSS clamping on 2026-03-06 02:20 UTC. - We merged a code change to bound streaming chunk sizes by default and added a feature flag to tune per-customer chunking (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/3372). - Added synthetic PMTU/streaming healthcheck to our SRE probes for dedicated pools in cross-region topologies. - Added runbook steps for networking team to check PMTU if streaming stalls are reported.
resolution: Mitigation and resolution implemented: transit provider enabled MSS clamping and restored PMTU signalling; we deployed a conservative default streaming chunk cap (1200 bytes) for the affected dedicated pool and released a per-customer config knob. Customer confirmed reduction to near-zero streaming stalls after 2026-03-06 03:00 UTC. Follow-ups: implement PMTU monitoring and automated fallbacks, add explicit MSS clamp detection alerts, include chunk-size test in onboarding for dedicated customers. Ticket closed after verification with customer and post-incident runbook created.
